name: Arch Capital Group Ltd.
executive_summary: Arch Capital is a Bermuda-domiciled specialty insurer/reinsurer/mortgage insurer trading at a deep earnings and book-value discount (screen: P/E 7.7×, P/B 1.6×, ROE 21.3%) despite sustained profitability and book-value compounding. FY2025 net income to common shareholders was $4.4bn on $16.5bn net premiums written, with book value per share rising to $65.11 (+23% YoY). The quantitative screen rates ACGL a strong buy (11/22 models; composite 86%), supported by cheapness, quality, GARP, and low leverage (D/E ~11%). The central debate is whether reinsurance pricing softening and catastrophe volatility will compress the earnings power that makes the stock look inexpensive, or whether disciplined underwriting, mortgage insurance, investment income, and buybacks will sustain returns through the cycle.
investment_thesis:
The screen’s strong-buy signal aligns with a business that combines specialty underwriting, a mortgage insurance franchise, and a large investment portfolio (~$47.4bn per FY2025 10-K). Arch passes 11 of 22 models across all four factor families—cheapness, quality, GARP, and risk—including Graham Enterprising, FCF Yield, Lynch PEG, Buffett Quality, and Economic Moat. At P/E 7.7× and P/B 1.6× against 21.3% ROE, the market prices ACGL as though peak-cycle earnings are already normalising, yet filings show continued underwriting profitability (group combined ratios mostly sub-82% in 2025 quarters) and tangible book growth.

Capital allocation reinforces the value case. The FY2025 10-K reports 455m shares repurchased for $7.8bn since 2007, with $1.1bn authorisation remaining at year-end; interim filings show accelerated repurchases ($813m in Q1 2026 alone). Low financial leverage (senior notes $2.7bn against $24.2bn shareholders’ equity at 31 March 2026) and minimal common dividends keep capital flexible. For a value investor, ACGL offers cyclical insurance exposure with screen-consistent metrics—high ROE, strong FCF ($5.3bn per screen; $6.1bn per Yahoo annual cash flow), and modest balance-sheet risk—at a multiple more typical of a mature commercial bank than a top-quartile underwriter.
financial_review:
**Annual results (10-K, SEC EDGAR)**

| Metric | FY2025 (10-K, filed Feb 2026) | FY2024 (10-K, filed Feb 2025) |
|---|---|---|
| Net premiums written | $16.5bn | $15.7bn |
| Net income to common shareholders | $4.4bn | $4.3bn |
| Book value per share | $65.11 | $53.11 |
| Prior-year BVPS | — | $46.94 (at 31 Dec 2023) |

Net premium growth was ~5% in 2025; net income was broadly flat YoY, but book value per share rose ~23%, driven by earnings retention, investment marks, and share count reduction. The FY2025 10-K cites an investment portfolio of ~$47.4bn (vs ~$41.4bn in FY2024), with emphasis on capital preservation and liquidity. Share repurchase authorisation stood at $1.1bn at 31 December 2025.

*Note:* Filing body extracts are truncated and do not include full consolidated income statements for the 10-K; annual revenue and segment combined ratios are not available in the extracted bodies. Total revenue FY2025 of $19.3bn (vs $16.9bn FY2024) is cited from Yahoo (`financials_annual.json`) as fallback only.

**Interim results (10-Q)**

*Q1 2026 (filed May 2026):*
- Net premiums earned: $3,986m (−4.8% vs $4,188m Q1 2025)
- Net income to common: $1,037m (+84% vs $564m)
- Diluted EPS: $2.88 (vs $1.48)
- Group combined ratio: **81.7%** (vs 90.1%)
- Net investment income: $408m (+7.9%)
- Net realised gains/(losses): **($87)m** (vs $3m gain prior year)
- Total assets: $81.4bn; shareholders’ equity: $24.2bn

Segment combined ratios (Q1 2026): Insurance 96.5%, Reinsurance 75.9%, Mortgage 22.3%; group 81.7%. Insurance remains the weakest segment.

*Q3 2025 (filed Nov 2025):*
- Q3 net income to common: $1,340m; diluted EPS $3.56
- 9M 2025 net income to common: **$3,131m** (−6.5% vs $3,347m 9M 2024)
- 9M net premiums earned: $12,810m (+16.9% vs $10,957m)
- 9M net investment income: $1,191m (+9.3%)
- Q3 group combined ratio: **79.8%**; 9M group combined ratio: **81.6%** (flat vs 81.6% 9M 2024)

*Q2 2025:* Group combined ratio **81.2%** (quarter).

*Q1 2025:* Group combined ratio **90.1%**, reflecting an elevated loss ratio (61.8%) in a heavier cat quarter.

**Trend assessment**

Premium growth moderated into Q1 2026 (net premiums earned down YoY), while underwriting profitability improved sharply as the loss ratio normalised. Nine-month 2025 earnings dipped slightly despite strong top-line growth, partly reflecting higher tax ($550m vs $296m) and foreign-exchange headwinds. Reserve development has been modestly favourable in recent quarters (e.g. Q1 2026 insurance segment: $10m favourable in travel/accident). Book value compounding remains the standout metric. Balance sheet expanded: total assets $81.4bn and loss reserves $34.1bn at 31 March 2026, consistent with premium scale-up.

**Gaps:** Eight 8-K filings in the index lack body extracts; no going-concern language was found in available bodies. Full annual segment combined ratios and operating ROE are not extractable from truncated 10-K bodies.
risks_and_flags:
**Catastrophe and reserve risk.** Filings repeatedly flag aggregate catastrophe exposure and the potential for adverse prior-year reserve development. Q1 2025’s 90.1% combined ratio illustrates earnings sensitivity to cat frequency. Q1 2026 net realised investment losses of $87m add mark-to-market volatility atop underwriting risk.

**Cycle and pricing.** The reinsurance group emphasises “disciplined underwriting over premium growth.” Q1 2026 net premiums earned declined YoY, an early signal of softer growth as industry pricing normalises—a theme echoed in external commentary (see News). Competition from alternative capital and increased pricing pressure are listed as explicit risk factors in every interim filing.

**Reinsurance credit and concentrations.** Recoverables on ceded business are material ($9.7bn at 31 March 2026). Filings warn that reinsurer defaults would leave Arch liable for ceded amounts; broker/reinsurer concentration is cross-referenced to contingencies notes.

**Tax and regulatory.** Bermuda corporate income tax and OECD Pillar II initiatives are cited as forward risks in all reviewed filings—relevant for a Bermuda-domiciled group with global operations. Climate-change considerations and thermal-coal policy are noted in the FY2025 10-K; no pension-related red flags appeared in available extracts.

**Governance and legal.** Item 1 (Legal Proceedings) and Item 3 (Defaults Upon Senior Securities) are referenced in 10-Q headers; body extracts contain no material litigation detail or covenant breach. Commitments and contingencies are noted on the balance sheet without quantified exposure in truncated bodies.

**Screen blind spots.** High ROE partly reflects elevated investment returns and favourable reserve releases; normalised ROE in a soft market with heavier cats could be materially lower, weakening the P/E case.
news_highlights:
Coverage over the past year is **thin on hard corporate events** and dominated by price action, earnings previews, and valuation commentary.

Material themes identified:

- **Reinsurance cycle concern:** *“Arch Capital: The Real Test Begins As Reinsurance Pricing Softens”* (Seeking Alpha, 17 Jul 2026) — flags the key fundamental debate.
- **Q2 2026 earnings preview:** *“Arch Capital to Report Q2 Earnings: What’s in Store for the Stock?”* (Yahoo Finance, 23 Jul 2026) — expects disciplined underwriting and higher investment income, but notes catastrophe losses and softer premium growth.
- **Capital return:** *“How The Arch Capital Group (ACGL) Story Is Shifting With Fresh Targets And Buybacks”* (Yahoo Finance, 10 Apr 2026).
- **Analyst action:** *“ACGL Maintained by JP Morgan — Price Target Raised to $116”* (GuruFocus, 20 Jul 2026).
- **Valuation debate:** Multiple articles (Jul 2026) argue shares remain cheap despite a 177% five-year return (*Yahoo Finance*, 18 Jul 2026).

No material M&A, CEO/CFO changes, or regulatory enforcement actions were identified in the manifest. Strategy references in filings (Coface 29.5% stake, Premia, Somerset Group acquisitions) pre-date the news window and are disclosed in 10-K business descriptions rather than recent headlines.
research_rationale: Filings confirm strong book-value growth, disciplined underwriting metrics, and aggressive buybacks that support the quantitative strong-buy signal, but moderating premium growth, cycle-turn rhetoric, and catastrophe sensitivity warrant a measured overlay rather than unqualified conviction.
